title: Multiplexed mid-stream model handoff and rate-window reconciliation
creator: Avery Lin
description:
Problem: we are observing cases where multiplexed clients (single TCP/WS session issuing concurrent streaming requests) change target models mid-stream (model handoff/fallback) while frames arrive out of order or are retransmitted. Current metering path attributes token counts too early to the initial model and to the per-connection rate window, which causes: 1) inaccurate per-model usage metrics, 2) doubled or dropped token credits when clients reconnect/resume, and 3) incorrect rate-limiter behavior for customers with tight quota windows, leading to throttling surprises.

This ticket proposes a deterministic reconciliation mechanism across the streaming pipeline so final token attribution and rate-window accounting reflect the true executed model and canonical ordering after stream finalization. The goal is strong correctness for billing and predictable rate-limiter behavior for multiplexed and interleaved streams without regressing latency for the common fast-path.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Final billing reports (per-customer, per-model) must match an offline golden-run within 0.1% for test traces that include mid-stream model switches and out-of-order frames.
2) Rate limiter should never double-charge or permanently lose tokens for resumed/multiplexed streams under simulated flaky networks.
3) No customer-facing increase in median tail latency >5% on a Canary (10k qps) when provisional accounting is enabled.
4) Automated end-to-end tests for 6 replay scenarios (model-swap, reconnect, duplicate frames, multiplexed interleaving, partial commit, early-cancel) must pass in CI.
5) Rollout plan executed with feature flag and monitoring dashboards green for 72h before GA.
technical_design:
1) Assign a deterministic fragment_id and logical sequence watermark at the gateway for every client frame. For multiplexed sessions, include a per-request session_nonce to distinguish concurrent requests.
2) Change the streaming metering pipeline to write provisional token deltas to a short-lived staging ledger (TTL 60s) instead of immediately committing to the canonical billing store. The ledger stores: fragment_id, session_nonce, provisional_token_count, provisional_model_hint, timestamp.
3) At stream finalization (explicit end or idle timeout), run a reconciliation worker that orders fragments by watermark, deduplicates retransmits, and computes final per-request token counts and model attribution. The reconciliation worker emits a single idempotent commit to the canonical ledger.
4) Integrate reconciliation output with rate-limit windows by computing an adjusted window delta and publishing it to the rate-limit service via the existing rate-limit API. The rate-limit service will accept provisional deltas but only apply final commits; provisional deltas will produce soft-deny thresholds for fast-path checks but not persistent quota changes.
5) Implement heuristics for mid-stream model handoff: if a confirmed model switch occurs mid-stream, prorate previous provisional tokens to the pre-switch model only up to the last confirmed frame associated with that model; subsequent tokens are attributed to the new model. If ambiguity remains after timeout, favor the model that produced the largest completed fragment token count to avoid billing surprises for short fallbacks.
6) Add visibility: add a per-request reconciliation status and audit_id to logs and the Console metering trace so ops and customers can inspect how final attribution was decided.
7) Performance: keep the fast-path unchanged for single-request non-multiplexed sessions by bypassing the staging ledger when watermark and sequence guarantees exist; default to provisional path only when multiplexing, model-handoff, or retransmit is detected.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal canary: enable feature-flag for 5% of internal traffic and 100% of test env traffic. Monitor billing diffs and rate-limit behavior for 48h.
2) External Canary: enable 1% of customer traffic with non-critical customers opted in. Run for 72h.
3) Expand to 25% after green.
4) Full GA once 72h stability observed and acceptance criteria met.
5) If anywhere green shows >0.5% delta on per-customer billing compared to legacy pipeline, auto-roll back and open incident.
6) Provide migration doc for Dedicated/Private deployments describing config toggles and expected data migration for legacy staging ledgers.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: fragment id generation, dedupe logic, prorating algorithm, idempotent commit semantics.
- Integration tests: simulate multiplexed session with 3 concurrent streams, model switch on stream 2, network retransmits and out-of-order frames; assert final ledger state and rate-window adjustments.
- Load test: 50k QPS streaming mix with 10% multiplexed sessions to measure staging ledger memory & reconciliation throughput.
- Fuzz tests: random frame drops, reordered delivery, duplicated frames to verify no double-credits.
- Billing validation: run offline recon tool to compare new pipeline results to golden traces for 1000 recorded production sessions (sanitized).
- Observability tests: verify reconciliation_id surfaces in Console traces and matches ledger commits.
monitoring:
Add the following dashboards and alerts: 1) Reconciliation lag histogram (alert if >95p >30s). 2) Provisional vs final token delta mismatch rate (alert if >0.2%). 3) Rate-limiter soft-deny frequency (alert if sudden spike during rollout). 4) Per-customer billing delta vs legacy pipeline for canaries. 5) Reconciliation error rate and idempotent commit failures.
Instrumentation: log reconciliation_id, fragment_count, provisional_tokens, final_tokens, model_attribution, and affected_rate_window_id for every reconciled request.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Staging ledger increases memory pressure on gateway. Mitigation: enforce TTL, shard by customer, and backpressure when staging occupancy > threshold.
- Risk: Reconciliation worker lag causes delayed billing commits. Mitigation: scale workers horizontally and expose internal backlog metrics; fall back to immediate commit for urgent customers (configurable).
- Risk: Complexity in rate-limiter integration might introduce transient over-allow. Mitigation: rate-limiter accepts provisional deltas as soft checks and only applies final commits to persistent quotas; add circuit-breaker to revert to legacy commit path if anomalies detected.
- Risk: Deterministic watermarking requires clock sync. Mitigation: use gateway-assigned monotonic counters per-session instead of relying on wall-clock timestamps.
open_questions: What TTL for provisional staging ledger balances eventual consistency vs memory (60s suggested)?
Should we support a forced immediate-commit override for enterprise customers who explicitly request deterministic near-real-time billing?
How do Dedicated/Private customers run the reconciliation worker? Should it be bundled as a container artifact or run in the control plane?
Edge case policy: tie-breaker rule for equal token counts across models when attribution is ambiguous — prefer fallback model or prior model?
